images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A low ivory card wall about the height of a tissue box stands across the back of a pale neutral tabletop, its top edge crisp and slightly fibrous. Mounted at its centre is a round matte graphite thermostat dial with a knurled bezel and a plain front of tick marks. The acid-lime element is the dial's pointer, set straight up to the middle. In front of the wall, four small graphite desks sit in an even row, each with a folded ivory note and a frosted glass cup. A small ivory jacket hangs over one desk chair, and a folded cardigan lies on another. Fine machining lines on the bezel and light dust along the wall top show the scale. Everything is balanced and comfortable. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama, captured mid-disaster. The same graphite dial is being turned hard, its acid-lime pointer frozen mid-swing with a blurred arc showing it has been yanked back and forth. The desks below are split. The two on the left are coated in white frost, their frosted glass cups cracked and the ivory jacket stiff over its chair. The two on the right shimmer in heat haze, their ivory notes curling and browned at the edges, and the cardigan has been flung onto the floor. A thin line of meltwater runs along the table between the zones. Frost crystals hang in the cold air and warm dust rises on the right, and both extremes trace straight back to the dial. Photorealistic photograph of a vast handcrafted miniature landscape diorama. A wide cracked plain stretches to a hazy horizon, split sharply down the middle. The left half lies under white frost and ice ridges, the right half is scorched and broken into dry, pale, curling plates. Along the dividing line runs the enormous ivory wall, now a crumbling ruin with gaps and fallen sections, and the graphite thermostat dial hangs off it at a tilt, its bezel cracked and front pitted. Toppled desks lie half frozen in ice on one side and half baked into the dry crust on the other. At the dividing line, a slim graphite regulator mast rig on three legs extends an acid-lime balancing arm over both zones, and a narrow band of even, neutral ground is spreading out from its base. Wide 16:9 panoramic frame. The main ruin anchors the left or centre foreground, terrain rolls back to a distant horizon on the upper third, and the lime recovery rig sits in the right midground. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: soft overcast late-afternoon daylight still falling from the upper left, with long soft shadows grounding the ruins and atmospheric haze fading distant forms into pale grey-green.
